events.title: EPA revokes methane emissions charge rule via Congressional Review Act
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized a rule revoking the "Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems" rule, effective immediately. Congress passed and President Trump signed a joint resolution of disapproval (H.J. Res. 35, Public Law 119-2) on March 14, 2025, nullifying the November 2024 EPA rule that implemented methane emissions reporting and compliance procedures for petroleum and natural gas facilities. The EPA removed the rule from the Code of Federal Regulations, eliminating reporting requirements and associated compliance procedures for affected industry segments.
events.why_relevant: Revocation of environmental emissions regulations reduces federal oversight of greenhouse gas reporting and methane reduction requirements, affecting climate policy and corporate accountability in fossil fuel industries.
events.basis: Congress has passed and the President has signed a joint resolution of disapproval under the Congressional Review Act (CRA) of the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) final rule titled, 'Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems.' Under the joint resolution and by operation of the CRA, the 2024 WEC Final Rule now has no legal force or effect.

events.title: GSA Seeks Comments on Information Collection for Public Space Use
events.summary: The General Services Administration (GSA) has issued a notice requesting public comments on the extension of an information collection requirement for the Application/Permit for Use of Space in Public Buildings and Grounds, GSA Form 3453. This form is used by the public to request the use of federal spaces for cultural, educational, or recreational activities. Comments are invited on the necessity, utility, and burden of this information collection, with a deadline for submission by May 13, 2025.
events.why_relevant: This notice affects public access to federal spaces, impacting cultural and educational activities and the regulatory burden on applicants.
